$comment: The app's OWN materials. NOT upstream OpenRocket's, which are read straight
out of its Databases.java. This file is the hand-edited one: a tool or a
person adds to it, and nothing regenerates over it.
scripts/sync-materials.mjs merges both into public/data/materials.generated.json,
the catalog the app fetches at run time. Nothing in src/ holds a material.
`kind` says why an entry is here, and the app itself does not care:
adhesive  - upstream has no adhesive at all, and a fin fillet is made of
nothing else, so the fillet picker had nothing to offer.
corrected - upstream carries the material but with a wrong number; both
are kept, because a design that names the upstream one has to
keep reading back the density it was saved with. A correction
takes its OWN name for that reason; one that reused upstream's
is refused by the sync script and by the extraction gate.
`density` is SI: kg/m^3 for bulk, kg/m^2 for surface, kg/m for line.
`source` and `note` are for whoever maintains this file. They are NOT
shipped to the app, and they are the whole reason an entry is trustworthy:
a density with no document behind it is a guess that weighs someone's
rocket. The sync script refuses an entry without a source. The same table,
with the links and the reasoning, is in
website/docs/designing-a-rocket.md#adhesives.

materials.name: Epoxy - West System 105/205 Fast
materials.note: Cured specific gravity 1.18, printed under Physical Properties of Cured Epoxy.

materials.name: Epoxy - West System Six10
materials.note: Cured specific gravity 1.18; components 1.17 resin and 1.04 hardener, 2:1 by volume.

materials.name: Epoxy - AeroPoxy PR2032/PH3660
materials.note: Cured 1.11. The bulletin tabulates PR2032 against four hardeners (PH3630 1.16, PH3660 1.11, PH3663 1.109, PH3665 1.12); PH3660 at 100:27 by weight is the one rocketry uses. PTM&W pulled the bulletins off the live site, hence the archive link.

materials.name: Epoxy - AeroPoxy ES6209
materials.note: Cured 1.09; components 1.10 resin and 0.98 hardener, 1:1 by weight or volume.

materials.name: Epoxy - RocketPoxy G5000
materials.note: The datasheet prints "Specific gravity mixed 1.50" outright (resin 1.52, hardener 1.48). Filled, hence the weight.

materials.name: Epoxy - TotalBoat High Performance
materials.note: MIXED LIQUID, not cured: resin 1.11 from the SDS, hardener ~1.00, 2:1 by volume. TotalBoat's published 100A:45B by weight against 2:1 by volume implies the same hardener density independently.

materials.name: Epoxy - BSI Quik/Mid/Slow-Cure
materials.note: MIXED LIQUID: the SDS gives the pair as "Specific gravity 0.97 / 1.15", identical across all three cure speeds, and they mix 1:1 by volume.

materials.name: Epoxy - J-B Weld Original
materials.note: MIXED LIQUID: Part A resin 1.78 (this SDS), Part B hardener 1.902 (https://media.napaonline.com/is/content/GenuinePartsCompany/2118182pdf), 1:1 by volume. Steel-filled, which is why it is 56% denser than West System and a poor fin fillet.

materials.name: Carpenter's glue (PVA, dried)
materials.note: DRIED film. Titebond III is 9.22 lb/gal (1105 kg/m3) wet at 52% solids, so the bead loses about half its volume drying and what is left is polyvinyl acetate at ~1.19. Model the bead you have after it dries.

materials.name: Elastic cord, corrected (flat 19 mm, 3/4 in)
materials.note: Upstream reads 0.0012 for this width, lighter than its own 0.0043 for a 6 mm cord: a dropped digit. mmrocket-sim found it and published 0.0123; interpolating upstream's own 6 mm and 12 mm entries gives 0.0127. Credited in engine-java/ATTRIBUTION.md.

materials.name: Elastic cord, corrected (flat 25 mm, 1 in)
materials.note: Upstream reads 0.0016, a dropped digit like the 19 mm above. mmrocket-sim publishes 0.016; interpolation of upstream's 6 mm and 12 mm gives 0.0167.
